[engine] A gate quantity computed at one call site and DISCARDED at another is not a gate quantity. Enforce it by funnelling every site through one counted entry point, not by adding a counter and hoping each caller reads it -- the caller that does not read it is exactly the caller the gate exists for.

<!-- generated by harness_engine/build_memories.py from traces/lessons.jsonl -->
<!-- lesson_id: eng-gate-0009 | class: gate-integrity | superseded_by: - -->

**class**: `gate-integrity`

## 為什麼（because）

llama_expert_cache_publish_slot_table returns the number of entries it had to clamp to 0 because the layer has no reserved ZERO slot, and §8.3 identified that count as the signal of a SILENT correctness failure: with zero_slot < 0 a non-resident selected expert makes the host leaf write -1 (loud -- the consumer reports an out-of-range id) while the table clamps it to 0 (index 0 is legal, so mul_mat_id reads a DIFFERENT expert's weights). There are exactly two call sites. The fast-path site checked the return value and printed it. The pool-path site discarded it outright -- and the pool path is the one EVERY MTP-off S1 arm actually takes, because CGC_SERVER_MTP=0 makes verify_fast and draft_fast both false so the `(verify_fast || draft_fast) && cgc_fast_eligible` guard is never entered. Every S1 measurement to date therefore computed the silent-corruption counter and threw it away. A second, independent divergence sat in the same pair: the two sites write the LEAF under different mappings (slot_table_safe vs the raw slot table) while publishing the TABLE through the same function, so their table/leaf equivalence is asserted, not shared.

## 反例（counterexample_observed）

A counter that is computed on every publish of the arm being measured, and read by nobody on that path.
